input.summary:
Atrium interior built in parts/room-5.mjs: a 2-wide smooth_stone slab path on x=19..20 between the doors, a jungle sapling tree as the focal piece (lit by three garden lamps), a 3-seat spruce stair bench on the east glass, grass tufts, a large fern and potted cacti.
make.sh runs clean with 52 blocks placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE. mcd room reports OK, walk ok, min light 10 with 0 dark cells.
The atrium's grass_block patch is not built: the shell locks the y=0 dirt, so the planting is short_grass on dirt.
left: Grass patch is short_grass tufts on the locked y=0 dirt, not a grass_block patch (the shell owns y=0 under the atrium); a grass_block patch would need the shell to lay grass there.
Stepping path is smooth_stone_slab (bottom, y=1) on x=19..20 rather than full smooth_stone, for the same reason: y=0 is locked, and a slab at y=1 keeps the path walkable.
Atrium planting item in elements.md (17) is only partly met: no rocks, no potted palm, no grass_block patch. Not ticked.
mcd check shows floating blocks at y=5 (x=14..18 and x=20..21, z=18..25) from the roof/ceiling parts not yet built, not from this module.
Did not render the whole house tiles (spec step 4); checked with mcd rooms (atrium from above and inside) instead.

waste.what: Worked out the 6x5 footprint for the atrium by hand: the x/z cell of every furniture, plant, lamp and tree part, one character per cell, then the y=2..4 layers for the lamps, fern and crown.
waste.cost: about 5 minutes of grid drafting and a few rewrites of the layer rows, across 4 y-layers of 6 rows each
waste.tool: mcd plan already prints the floor grid; a layers() preview that prints each y-layer with the same characters, or a helper that places a jungle tree or garden lamp from one (x, z) and a height, would have saved the hand-drawn crowns and lamp posts.

waste.what: Re-declared MCD=... in every shell call, and ran the room check, the structure check and the rooms render as separate Bash calls.
waste.tool: a `mcd room` / `mcd rooms` pair that writes the walk, light and PNG in one run would cut this to one call.
